title: Inquest called in North York man's 2004 death
article: An inquest into the death of a man at a North York hospital three years ago while in police custody has been announced by an Ontario coroner.
Dr. James Edwards, regional supervising coroner for Toronto East, announced that an inquest will be held into the death of Antonio Bellon.
Bellon, 64, died at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre Jan. 10, 2004, while in the custody of Toronto Police. Under the Coroner's
Act, an inquest is mandatory when a person dies while in custody.
The inquest will review the events surrounding Bellon's death and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths in similar circumstances.
The inquest will begin at 9:30 a.m. Aug. 20 at the Toronto Coroners Courts, 15 Grosvenor St. Dr. Richard Isaac will preside as inquest coroner and Lorna Spencer will act as counsel to the coroner.
